gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patient previously diagnosed with WHO grade 4 IDH-wildtype GBM, determined through genomic and/or histopathological analysis.

candidate_evidence.quote: [EXPERIMENTAL] Pembrolizumab + focused ultrasound sonication: Pembrolizumab along with focused ultrasound sonication following surgery for recurrent glioblastoma.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Treatment of Recurrent WHO Grade 4 IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma With Mismatch Repair Deficiency

flag.reason: Pembrolizumab is the only antitumour drug, but it is combined with a focused ultrasound device (with microbubbles) for BBB opening; device is not a drug or radiotherapy so coded monotherapy.

role_evidence.quote: Treatment dosing will be 200mg of pembrolizumab every three weeks for up to six months or until disease progression, whichever occurs first.

patients will received NaviFUS sonication to the complete volume of the tumor resection bed (as limited by anatomic constraints relative to the tumor extension) following microbubble (Bracco Imaging, SonoVue® or Lumason®; 0.1 mL/Kg; maximum 4.8 mL) administration

agents.drug_class_hint: ultrasound contrast agent used with focused ultrasound for blood-brain barrier opening

flag.reason: Microbubbles are part of the device procedure and not a separately registered intervention; role coded supportive with delivery_enabling true as no other role fits.

source_quote.quote: MMR deficiencies confirmed per standard of care immunohistochemical analysis or Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) of the patient's surgical sample from the time of initial GBM diagnosis or recurrence.
Patient previously diagnosed with WHO grade 4 IDH-wildtype GBM, determined through genomic and/or histopathological analysis.
To evaluate levels of baseline tumor markers related to immune and genetic repair function, including PD-L1, microsatellite instability (MSI), and tumor mutational burden (TMB).

coder_notes: MMR deficiency is an eligibility requirement and is mechanistically linked to the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab (MMR-d/hypermutation as rationale for checkpoint inhibition), so candidate_matched_selection should be true. Focused ultrasound (NaviFUS device) with microbubbles is a BBB-opening device intervention, not a drug candidate. Collaborator NaviFUS Corporation (device company).
